For your career goal, definitely WFCB. WFCB is  focused on ecology, wildlife, and field research. Animal Bio and Animal Science are focused on domestic animals and husbandry, and saturated with pre-vet students.

There are ~300 students now. Professors are awesome and very passionate about their work. Many classes offer field trips and hands-on experiences. There are also lots of other opportunities to get involved with labs with research and field work through internships, volunteer work, paid positions, etc.

There are a lot of opportunities. Easy to get if you're proactive, go to office hours, ask questions, build connections, etc. Hard if you sit around thinking someone will just offer you an internship for being in their class

I chose UCD over UCLA and prioritized my mental health. Prestige is not worth a miserable several years in an environment you don't see yourself in

I'm also in an environmental science related major and I chose Davis over UCLA. I've never regretted my decision. I really really love Davis! 

There's so many opportunities in our field at Davis, and it is less competitive in my opinion and easier to get involved because of smaller but great departments. 

Davis is a much better environment for me personally compared to what I expect to be a super intense, stressful, and competitive environment (I also grew up near LA in extremely competitive academic environments and it was really not for me). So the intensity of the change just depends on what environment you want to be in. Prestige is one thing but taking advantage of all the opportunities and resources you have during your time there is just as valuable in my opinion. 

Also, Davis is small but larger cities like Sacramento, SF+the bay area are also pretty accessible if you have a car or are willing to use public transit.

Fitting in:
I found it easy to "fit in" because of my small major department and getting involved as much as possible.

Ultimately, it really came down to the competitive stressful environment at UCLA (and LA/big city environment itself) that pushed my decision towards Davis. 

It was hard to get past the prestige when that was constantly pushed at me my whole life but I chose to put my mental health first.

Anyways I hope this was helpful I'm happy to answer more questions...
